html:
The founding of Byzantium on the European shore of the Bosporus by colonists from Megara, dated to around 657 BCE. Legend names their leader Byzas.

The site was superb: a hilly point with a deep sheltered harbour, the Golden Horn, at the narrow strait between the Black Sea and the Mediterranean. Herodotus tells that a Persian general called the people of Chalcedon, founded earlier on the opposite Asian shore, blind for missing it. Later writers turned this into advice from the Oracle of Delphi to settle "opposite the blind".

Byzantium grew rich by taxing ships carrying Black Sea grain, and Athens, Sparta and Persia fought over it. It was part of the wider wave of Greek colonisation. In 330 CE Constantine refounded it as Constantinople, capital of the eastern Roman Empire, and it later became Istanbul.
sum: The founding of Byzantium on the European shore of the Bosporus by colonists from Megara, dated to around 657 BCE. Legend names their leader Byzas.
